title: He preached God’s truth—
paragraphs:
He preached God’s truth—
and felt betrayed by the very God who called him.

Jeremiah said it raw:
“O Lord, thou hast deceived me, and I was deceived…”
That is not polished faith.
That is wounded obedience.
That is the emotional weight of a man carrying a word too heavy for his own chest.
Jeremiah 20:7 is what it sounds like when calling costs more than comfort.

He was mocked.
Ignored.
Laughed at.
Every sermon felt like a setup for suffering.
He opened his mouth for God, and pain came rushing in.
And some of us know that feeling.

You prayed and still broke.
You obeyed and still got betrayed.
You stayed clean, stayed faithful, stayed available—
and somehow the burden got heavier, not lighter.

That’s where Jeremiah meets us.
Not in the shallow waters of easy inspiration.
But in the deep place where ministry hurts.
Where obedience feels lonely.
Where the soul whispers, “Lord… this is too much.”

Jeremiah did not stop bringing his pain to God.
He brought the complaint into the presence of the One who called him.
He wrestled honestly, not rebelliously.
And that kind of honesty is not unbelief.
It is the cry of a heart still facing heaven.

This is the mercy of Scripture:
God did not erase Jeremiah’s anguish from the record.
He preserved it.

Because the Lord is not scared of the tears of His servants.
He is not threatened by trembling voices.
He does not discard broken prophets.
He holds them.
And Jeremiah’s pain points us forward to Someone greater.

Jesus also carried the crushing weight of obedience.
He was rejected by men.
Misunderstood.
Mocked.
A Man of sorrows, acquainted with grief.
Where Jeremiah felt the fire of the word in his bones, Christ became the Word made flesh and carried the cross all the way to Calvary.

So when the calling feels heavy, do not think you are abandoned.
When the assignment wounds you, do not assume God has left the room.
And when your soul is tired enough to speak like Jeremiah, remember: the Savior knows that weight too.

Your pain is not proof that God failed you.
Sometimes it is proof that you are carrying something eternal in a world that resists light.

Bring Him the ache.
Bring Him the confusion.
Bring Him the exhausted “why.”
And let Jesus meet you there.

Because grace is not only for your sin.
Grace is also for your weariness.
